plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A cormous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers in autumn with no leaves present. The strap-shaped leaves appear in spring and die back by summer, giving rise to the nickname 'naked ladies'. All parts are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Temperate Europe, damp meadows and woodland edges; widely cultivated in gardens in North America and elsewhere
plants.funFact: It contains colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling. It is not related to true crocuses or the saffron crocus.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, bushy native wildflower with hairy stems and masses of daisy-like flower heads featuring many narrow ray petals around yellow centers. It thrives in moist meadows, roadsides, and prairies, and is an important late-season nectar source.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Quebec to the Rocky Mountains and south to Alabama
plants.funFact: Its blooms are a critical fuel stop for migrating monarch butterflies heading to Mexico, which often pass through in late September.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: A bulbous perennial producing umbels of spidery, wavy-petaled, sparkly flowers on bare stems in autumn. The petals have a glistening, frosted texture, and strap-like leaves follow the flowers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early autumn to early winter (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Drakensberg mountains of South Africa; widely grown in gardens in the UK, Europe, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Although native to South Africa, where September is spring, it adapted to flower in autumn in the Northern Hemisphere, and it thrives in the heat-baked, sunny base of walls.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular deciduous tree with fern-like leaves that erupts into clouds of lavender-blue, trumpet-shaped flowers just before leaf flush. Fallen blossoms carpet streets and pavements in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (September to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina, and Brazil
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed 'Jacaranda City' for its tens of thousands of trees, and in Australia, folklore says a blossom falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody shrub with large, bowl-shaped flower heads composed of a central cone of tiny flowers surrounded by showy, petal-like bracts. It grows on rocky slopes of the fynbos and is a popular cut flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak bloom around September to November
plants.location: Fynbos regions of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower, and its fire-adapted stems have underground lignotubers that allow resprouting after wildfires.
